snapshot.summary: Submit quarterly reports to the council and mayor, and post to the department's website, containing data on criminal and civil summonses issued, disaggregated by offense, race, gender, age, borough, precinct, and service area.
snapshot.deadline_text: within 30 days of the beginning of each quarter
snapshot.quote: The commissioner shall submit to the council and the mayor, and post to the department's website, within 30 days of the beginning of each quarter, a report containing the following information for the previous quarter

snapshot.summary: Store summons report information permanently on the department's website in a format that permits automated processing and includes comparisons to prior quarters and years.
snapshot.quote: The information required pursuant to subdivisions a and b for each quarter shall be stored permanently on the department's website and shall be provided in a format that permits automated processing.

snapshot.summary: Complete a survey of each firehouse to determine permanent upgrades that would facilitate use by a mixed gender workforce, considering privacy provided by bathrooms, bunkrooms, locker rooms, changing areas, and other relevant areas.
snapshot.deadline_text: No later than June 30, 2024
snapshot.quote: the department shall complete a survey of each firehouse to determine the permanent upgrades that would facilitate use by a mixed gender workforce. In conducting such survey, the department shall consider the privacy provided by the layout and location of bathrooms, bunkrooms, locker rooms, changing areas and any other relevant areas of the firehouse.

snapshot.summary: Implement interim measures, such as physical barriers, as practicable, to accommodate a mixed gender workforce at each surveyed firehouse.
snapshot.quote: the department shall implement interim measures, such as, but not limited to, physical barriers, as practicable, to accommodate a mixed gender workforce.

snapshot.summary: Submit to the mayor and the speaker of the council a report on survey findings detailing permanent facility upgrades that would facilitate use by a mixed gender workforce, feasibility of implementation at each firehouse, construction plans, and interim measures taken.
snapshot.deadline_text: Upon completion of the survey required by subdivision a of this section
snapshot.quote: the department shall submit to the mayor and the speaker of the council a report on the findings of the survey detailing the permanent facility upgrades that would facilitate use by a mixed gender workforce, as well as the feasibility of implementing such permanent upgrades at each firehouse. The report shall provide information related to any construction plans to make such upgrades and what, if any, interim measures have been taken at any such firehouses.

snapshot.summary: Create a centralized electronic system to track all city-issued parking permits and record all summonses issued in connection with improper use of such permits, enabling real-time verification of permit validity.
snapshot.quote: The department shall create a centralized electronic system to track all city-issued parking permits and to record all summonses issued by the department in connection with the improper use of city-issued parking permits. Such system shall allow the department to verify in real time the validity of city-issued parking permits.

snapshot.summary: Provide information about city-issued parking permits to the department, including the vehicles and permissible and non-permissible locations and uses associated with such permits.
snapshot.quote: The department of transportation and the department of education, if authority to issue city-issued parking permits is delegated pursuant to section 19-162.3, shall provide the department with information about city-issued parking permits to be included in the electronic system, including but not limited to the vehicle or vehicles and the permissible and non-permissible locations and uses associated with such permit.

snapshot.summary: Provide information about city-issued parking permits to the department, including the vehicles and permissible and non-permissible locations and uses associated with such permits, if authority to issue such permits is delegated to the department of education.
snapshot.quote: The department of transportation and the department of education, if authority to issue city-issued parking permits is delegated pursuant to section 19-162.3, shall provide the department with information about city-issued parking permits to be included in the electronic system, including but not limited to the vehicle or vehicles and the permissible and non-permissible locations and uses associated with such permit.

snapshot.summary: Report each month on summonses issued for misuse of a city-issued parking permit to the city agency whose employee was issued the permit.
snapshot.quote: The department shall report each month on summonses issued for misuse of a city-issued parking permit to the city agency whose employee was issued the permit for which the summons was issued.

snapshot.summary: Submit to the speaker of the council and post on the department's website a biannual report on the duration of general and special education school bus routes, categorized by completion time and disaggregated by community school district.
snapshot.deadline_text: Beginning October 31, 2019, and on or before each April 30 and October 31 thereafter
snapshot.quote: Beginning October 31, 2019, and on or before each April 30 and October 31 thereafter, the department shall submit to the speaker of the council and post on the department's website a report for the relevant reporting period

snapshot.summary: Submit to the speaker of the council a biannual report on scheduled and actual arrival and departure times for general and special education school bus routes, including school bus vendor information.
snapshot.deadline_text: Beginning April 30, 2020, and on or before each October 31 and April 30 thereafter
snapshot.quote: Beginning April 30, 2020, and on or before each October 31 and April 30 thereafter, the department shall submit to the speaker of the council for the relevant reporting period, as defined in section 21-993, the scheduled arrival and departure times for each transportation site, and data points, including the time of day corresponding with the actual arrival at the first and last transportation site of each special education school bus route and general education school bus route for each day of the reporting period. Such information shall also include the school bus vendor.

snapshot.summary: Submit a report to the mayor, the speaker of the council, and the department including results of its study and any recommendations, no later than January 31, 2024, and annually on January 31 thereafter.
snapshot.deadline_text: No later than January 31, 2024, and annually on January 31 thereafter
snapshot.quote: No later than January 31, 2024, and annually on January 31 thereafter, the advisory board shall submit a report to the mayor, the speaker of the council, and the department including the results of its study and any recommendations required by this section.

snapshot.summary: Appoint 4 of the 7 public members of the shelter accessibility advisory board.
snapshot.quote: 4 of whom shall be appointed by the mayor and 3 of whom shall be appointed by the speaker of the council

snapshot.summary: Promulgate rules establishing the form and manner for submission of workforce disclosure records by covered developers and contractors.
snapshot.quote: The information required by subdivision a of this section shall be submitted electronically to the administering agency in a form and manner to be determined by the administering agency.

snapshot.summary: Make data received from covered developers pursuant to section 22-1102 publicly available online in anonymized form.
snapshot.deadline_text: By no later than October 31, 2021
snapshot.quote: By no later than October 31, 2021, the administering agency shall make data received pursuant to section 22-1102 of this chapter publicly available online where such data can be anonymized.

snapshot.summary: Designate in writing one or more offices or agencies to administer and enforce the provisions of this chapter, and publish such designation and any changes thereto on the city's website and on the website of each such office or agency within 10 days, with electronic submission to the speaker of the council.
snapshot.deadline_text: Within 10 days after such designation or change thereof
snapshot.quote: The mayor shall, in writing, designate one or more offices or agencies to administer and enforce the provisions of this chapter and may, from time to time at the mayor's discretion, change such designation. Within 10 days after such designation or change thereof, a copy of such designation or change thereof shall be published on the city's website and on the website of each such office or agency, and shall be electronically submitted to the speaker of the council.

snapshot.summary: Provide notice of potential eligibility for tax abatement to each identified landlord at least 2 times each year, in a form and manner determined by the agency, which may be provided electronically.
snapshot.quote: The responsible agency shall provide a notice of potential eligibility in accordance with this subdivision to each identified landlord at least 2 times each year, in a form and manner determined by the responsible agency.

snapshot.summary: Include information regarding program tax benefits with the notice of potential eligibility provided to identified landlords.
snapshot.quote: The responsible agency shall include information regarding program tax benefits with such notice.

snapshot.summary: Provide a renewal information notice to each identified head of household regarding renewal requirements for program rent benefits at least 60 days before expiration of a rent exemption order, where the head of household has not yet submitted a renewal application.
snapshot.deadline_text: at least 60 days before the expiration of a rent exemption order
snapshot.quote: The responsible agency shall provide a renewal information notice to each identified head of household regarding the renewal requirements for program rent benefits at least 60 days before the expiration of a rent exemption order, where such identified head of household has not yet submitted an applicable renewal application.

snapshot.summary: Include with the renewal information notice either applicable renewal application forms for program rent benefits or the address of the website containing such forms, the address where forms are available in-person, and instructions for requesting such forms via telephone.
snapshot.quote: The responsible agency shall either include the applicable renewal application forms for program rent benefits with such notice or include in such notice the address of the website containing such forms, the address of the responsible agency's office where such forms are available in-person, and instructions for requesting such forms via telephone.

snapshot.summary: Maintain a record of all third party notice designations submitted by identified heads of household.
snapshot.quote: The responsible agency shall maintain a record of all such third party notices.

snapshot.summary: Provide the renewal information notice to a third party designated by an identified head of household when such notice is sent to the head of household.
snapshot.quote: The responsible agency shall provide the renewal information notice to a third party designated pursuant to paragraph (1) of this subdivision when such notice is sent to an identified head of household pursuant to subdivision c of this section.

snapshot.summary: Send a notice to a surviving member of a household that may be eligible for a transferred program rent benefit if the agency identifies, based on available data, that such benefit may be transferred upon the death or permanent exit of an identified head of household.
snapshot.quote: If the responsible agency identifies, based on a review of available data, that a program rent benefit may be transferred pursuant to subdivision 4-a of section 467-b of the real property tax law, the responsible agency shall send a notice to a surviving member of the household that the responsible agency has determined, based on available data, may be eligible for such benefit.

snapshot.summary: Provide a renewal information notice to each identified head of household regarding renewal requirements for program rent benefits at least 60 days before expiration of a rent increase exemption order, where the head of household has not yet submitted a renewal application.
snapshot.deadline_text: at least 60 days before the expiration of a rent increase exemption order
snapshot.quote: The responsible agency shall provide a renewal information notice to each identified head of household regarding the renewal requirements for program rent benefits at least 60 days before the expiration of a rent increase exemption order, where such identified head of household has not yet submitted an applicable renewal application.

snapshot.summary: Include information regarding program tax benefits and PILOT exemptions with the notice of potential eligibility provided to identified landlords.
snapshot.quote: The responsible agency shall include information regarding program tax benefits and PILOT exemptions with such notice.

snapshot.summary: Send a notice to a surviving member of a household that may be eligible for a transferred program rent benefit if the agency identifies, based on available data, that such benefit may be transferred upon the death or permanent exit of an identified head of household.
snapshot.quote: If the responsible agency identifies, based on a review of available data, that a program rent benefit may be transferred pursuant to subdivision 4-a of section 467-c of the real property tax law, the responsible agency shall send a notice to a surviving member of the household that the responsible agency has determined, based on available data, may be eligible for such benefit.

snapshot.summary: Promulgate rules establishing the content of stormwater pollution prevention plans, consistent with the NYSDEC construction general permit.
snapshot.quote: Set forth the content of SWPPPs, , including identifying those development projects requiring only erosion and sediment controls during construction and those development projects requiring erosion and sediment controls and post-construction stormwater management facilities.

snapshot.summary: Promulgate rules establishing design standards for erosion and sediment controls and post-construction stormwater management facilities.
snapshot.quote: Establish design standards for erosion and sediment controls and post-construction stormwater management facilities [, which shall not be less stringent than the standards set forth or incorporated by reference in the NYSDEC construction general permit].

snapshot.summary: Promulgate rules establishing exemptions from permit requirements.
snapshot.quote: Establish exemptions from permit requirements, .

snapshot.summary: Promulgate rules providing for the regulation of development activity of less than one acre based on soil disturbance or impervious surface, where the department determines an appropriate reduction in threshold is necessary.
snapshot.quote: [After completion of the lot size soil disturbance study required by the NYC MS4 permit, provide] Provide for the regulation of development activity of less than one acre, based either on total disturbance of soil or on amount of impervious surface created or replaced, where the department determines an appropriate reduction in the threshold is necessary [in accordance with the NYC MS4 permit] to carry out the purposes of this chapter.

snapshot.summary: Promulgate rules establishing training, experience, and education requirements for qualified professionals and qualified inspectors.
snapshot.quote: Establish training, experience and/or education requirements for qualified professionals and qualified inspectors [, which shall not be less stringent than those required by the NYSDEC construction general permit].

snapshot.summary: Promulgate rules establishing procedures and fees for review of stormwater pollution prevention plans and issuance and renewal of permits.
snapshot.quote: Establish procedures and fees for the review of SWPPPs and the issuance and renewal of permits required by this subchapter.

snapshot.summary: Promulgate rules establishing record keeping, inspection, and reporting requirements for applicants and permittees to monitor compliance.
snapshot.quote: Establish record keeping, inspection and reporting requirements for applicants and permittees to monitor compliance with this subchapter and approved SWPPPs.

snapshot.summary: Promulgate rules establishing requirements for compliance certifications by contractors to be included with stormwater pollution prevention plans.
snapshot.quote: Establish requirements for compliance certifications by contractors to be included with SWPPPs.

snapshot.summary: Promulgate rules establishing standards for maintenance, inspection, repair, and replacement of required erosion and sediment controls and post-construction stormwater management facilities.
snapshot.quote: Establish standards for the maintenance, inspection, repair and replacement of required erosion and sediment controls and post-construction stormwater management facilities.

snapshot.summary: Review stormwater pollution prevention plans within time periods specified in rules and issue stormwater construction permits or MS4 SWPPP acceptance forms as appropriate.
snapshot.quote: The department or a qualified professional designated by the department shall review the SWPPP within time periods to be specified in the rules of the department.

snapshot.summary: Issue stormwater construction permits to developers upon acceptance of stormwater pollution prevention plans and all requested documentation.
snapshot.quote: If the department accepts the SWPPP and all other requested documentation, the department shall issue a stormwater construction permit to the developer and, for MS 4 projects subject to the NYSDEC construction general permit, shall issue an MS4 SWPPP acceptance form for filing with NYSDEC.

snapshot.summary: Send notice to developers indicating specific deficiencies when rejecting a stormwater pollution prevention plan.
snapshot.quote: If the department rejects the SWPPP the department shall send notice of such rejection to the developer indicating the specific deficiencies that caused the department to reject the SWPPP.

snapshot.summary: Not issue a stormwater construction permit until execution and recording of a maintenance easement binding on all subsequent owners of real property served by post-construction stormwater management facilities, except where the corporation counsel determines such easement is unnecessary.
snapshot.quote: the department shall not issue a stormwater construction permit for the project until the execution and recording of a maintenance easement, which shall be binding on all subsequent owners of the real property served by such post-construction stormwater management facility, except where the corporation counsel has determined that such a maintenance easement is not necessary due to the property's ownership or use by a public agency or instrumentality.

snapshot.summary: Ensure easement provides for access to post-construction stormwater management facilities at reasonable times for periodic inspection by the department or qualified professionals to ensure facilities are maintained in good working condition.
snapshot.quote: The easement shall provide for access to post-construction stormwater management facilities at reasonable times in accordance with law for periodic inspection by the department or qualified professionals authorized by the department to ensure that such facilities are maintained in good working condition to meet the applicable design standards.

snapshot.summary: May suspend or revoke a stormwater construction permit after notice and an opportunity for a hearing when there is substantial non-compliance with the law, rules, permit, or approved stormwater pollution prevention plan.
snapshot.quote: The department may suspend or revoke a stormwater construction permit, after notice and the opportunity for a hearing in accordance with the rules of the department, when the department or, in the case of an MS 4 project, NYSDEC finds that there is substantial non-compliance with this subchapter, the rules of the department, the NYSDEC construction general permit or the SWPPP, including any major change to erosion or sediment controls or any change in a post-construction stormwater management facility during construction that has or could have an effect on the discharge of pollutants, or when a permit was issued in error and conditions are such that a permit should not have been issued.

snapshot.summary: Promulgate rules relating to the granting of licenses and revocable consents for sidewalk and roadway cafes, the administration of such licenses and consents, the design of sidewalk and roadway cafes, priorities among applicants, and operation and maintenance standards.
snapshot.citation: Section 6 of the local law (NYC Admin. Code § 19-160(b))
snapshot.quote: the department, consistent with chapter 14 of the charter and the provisions of this subchapter, shall promulgate rules relating to (i) the granting of such licenses and revocable consents, and the administration of such licenses and revocable consents; (ii) the design of a sidewalk cafe or roadway cafe; (iii) priorities among applicants

snapshot.summary: Provide notice of petitions for revocable consents for roadway cafes to affected community boards and council members and provide opportunity for comment.
snapshot.citation: Section 6 of the local law (NYC Admin. Code § 19-160.1(e))
snapshot.quote: The department shall provide notice of a petition for a revocable consent for a roadway cafe to the affected community board and council member, and, to the extent practicable, provide an opportunity for both the community board and council member to submit comments to the department

snapshot.summary: Forward complete petitions for sidewalk cafes to the borough president, council speaker, council member, and community board within 5 days of receipt.
snapshot.citation: Section 6 of the local law (NYC Admin. Code § 19-160.2(a))
snapshot.deadline_text: within 5 days of the filing of such complete and accurate petition
snapshot.quote: the department shall, within 5 days of the filing of such complete and accurate petition, forward such petition by electronic mail to the president of the borough in which the cafe is proposed to be located, the speaker of the council and the council member in whose district the cafe is proposed to be located, for information purposes, and to the community board for the community district in which the cafe is proposed to be located, for review

snapshot.summary: Approve, disapprove, or approve with modifications petitions for sidewalk cafes within 20 days after the expiration of the community board review period.
snapshot.citation: Section 6 of the local law (NYC Admin. Code § 19-160.2(c)(1))
snapshot.deadline_text: within 20 days after the expiration of the period allowed for the filing of a recommendation or waiver by the community board
snapshot.quote: within 20 days after the expiration of the period allowed for the filing of a recommendation or waiver by the community board pursuant to subdivision b of this section, the department shall (i) approve the petition for a sidewalk cafe, disapprove it or approve it with modifications; and (ii) file with the council any such decision to approve or approve with modifications

snapshot.summary: Hold a public hearing on petitions for sidewalk cafes when required by law and render approval, disapproval, or approval with modifications decisions within 30 or 45 days.
snapshot.citation: Section 6 of the local law (NYC Admin. Code § 19-160.2(c)(2))
snapshot.deadline_text: within 30 days after the expiration of the period allowed for the filing of a recommendation or waiver by the community board pursuant to subdivision b of the section, or within 45 days after the expiration of such period when the department plans to combine the public hearing on the petition
snapshot.quote: If the department holds such a public hearing, within 30 days after the expiration of the period allowed for the filing of a recommendation or waiver by the community board pursuant to subdivision b of the section, or within 45 days after the expiration of such period when the department plans to combine the public hearing on the petition with the public hearing required on 1 or more additional petitions pursuant to paragraph 3 of this subdivision, the department shall (i) hold a public hearing on the petition

snapshot.summary: Give notice at least 15 days prior to holding a public hearing on sidewalk cafe petitions to the community board, borough president, and council member.
snapshot.citation: Section 6 of the local law (NYC Admin. Code § 19-160.2(d))
snapshot.deadline_text: At least 15 days prior to the date of a hearing
snapshot.quote: At least 15 days prior to the date of a hearing held pursuant to paragraph 2 of subdivision c of this section, the department will give notice to the community board for the district in which the cafe is proposed to be located, to the president of the borough in which the cafe is proposed to be located and to the council member in whose district the cafe is proposed to be located.

snapshot.summary: Publish notice of sidewalk cafe petition hearings in the City Record and in print or online editions of local newspapers at least 5 calendar days prior to the hearing.
snapshot.citation: Section 6 of the local law (NYC Admin. Code § 19-160.2(d))
snapshot.deadline_text: Not less than 5 calendar days prior to the date of any such hearing
snapshot.quote: Not less than 5 calendar days prior to the date of any such hearing, notice of the hearing shall be published in the City Record and in the print or online edition of 1 newspaper of local circulation in the community where the cafe is proposed to be located.

snapshot.summary: Notify license holders of first-time violations and request corrective action within 30 days, and afford opportunity to contest the finding.
snapshot.citation: Section 6 of the local law (NYC Admin. Code § 19-160.5(e))
snapshot.deadline_text: within 30 days
snapshot.quote: if the department finds that any holder of a license to operate a sidewalk cafe or roadway cafe has violated for the first time (i) any provision of section 19-160 through 19-160.6 or any rule promulgated thereunder, or (ii) the terms or conditions of such license, the department shall notify such license holder of such violation and request that action be taken to correct such violation within 30 days and shall afford such licensee an opportunity to contest the department's finding

snapshot.summary: Submit a report on compensation for revocable consents for sidewalk and roadway cafes by May 1, 2027 and every 4 years thereafter.
snapshot.citation: Section 6 of the local law (NYC Admin. Code § 19-160.7)
snapshot.deadline_text: No later than May 1, 2027, and every 4 years thereafter
snapshot.quote: No later than May 1, 2027, and every 4 years thereafter, the commissioner shall submit a report to the speaker of the council and the mayor on the changes to the median annual rent charged for a ground floor commercial premises for each sector, the corresponding percent land area for each sector, the number of restaurants operating sidewalk and/or roadway cafes in each sector, and the square footage of each sidewalk and roadway cafe in operation.

snapshot.summary: Establish a permanent open restaurants program including the use of roadway seating for outdoor dining and accessibility for people with disabilities.
snapshot.citation: Section 8, amending Local Law 114 of 2020 (subdivision b of section 2)
snapshot.quote: The department of transportation [and any other agency designated by the mayor] shall establish a permanent open restaurants program to succeed the temporary program established by local law number 77 for the year 2020[, provided that any additional legislation necessary to authorize such program has been enacted]. Such program shall include but not be limited to the following elements: 1. The use of roadway seating for outdoor dining; and 2. [The use of a pedestrian plaza, or other public outdoor location for outdoor dining; and 3.] Accessibility for people with disabilities in compliance with applicable federal, state and local law.

snapshot.summary: Develop a map on the department's website showing the location and name of each restaurant with a license and revocable consent for sidewalk or roadway cafes, required drawings, and inspection history.
snapshot.deadline_text: Within 12 months of the effective date of section 19-160 of the administrative code of the city of New York, as added by section six of this local law
snapshot.quote: Within 12 months of the effective date of section 19-160 of the administrative code of the city of New York, as added by section six of this local law, the department of transportation shall develop a map on its website that shows the location and name of each restaurant that has obtained a license and revocable consent to operate a sidewalk cafe or a roadway cafe; a copy of the drawing required to be submitted with the petition for a revocable consent for a roadway cafe pursuant to the rules of the department; a copy of the drawing required to be submitted with the petition for a revocable consent for a sidewalk cafe pursuant to subdivision a of section 19-160.2 of the administrative code of the city of New York, as added by section six of this local law, and a history of any inspections of such sidewalk cafe or roadway cafe by such department.

snapshot.summary: Submit an annual report to the mayor and speaker of the council for 4 years specifying the total number of sidewalk and roadway cafes licensed, disaggregated by borough, and the total number of inspections and summonses issued.
snapshot.deadline_text: Within 12 months of the effective date of section 19-160 of the administrative code of the city of New York, as added by section six of this local law, and annually thereafter for 4 years
snapshot.quote: Within 12 months of the effective date of section 19-160 of the administrative code of the city of New York, as added by section six of this local law, and annually thereafter for 4 years, the department of transportation shall submit to the mayor and to the speaker of the council a report. Such report shall specify the total number of sidewalk cafes and roadway cafes licensed by such department, disaggregated by borough, and the total number of inspections performed and summonses issued by such department in the preceding 12-month period.

snapshot.summary: Convene a working group task force to facilitate the transition of authority from the department of consumer and worker protection to the department of transportation for granting licenses and revocable consents for sidewalk cafes.
snapshot.deadline_text: Such task force shall hold its first meeting no later than 30 days after the effective date of this section, and shall thereafter meet no less than quarterly until March 31, 2025
snapshot.quote: The department of transportation shall convene a working group task force to facilitate the transition of authority from the department of consumer and worker protection to the department of transportation for the granting of licenses and revocable consents for sidewalk cafes. Such task force shall consist of members of the department of transportation, the department of consumer and worker protection, and the department of city planning, as designated by the commissioner of each such department. Such task force shall hold its first meeting no later than 30 days after the effective date of this section, and shall thereafter meet no less than quarterly until March 31, 2025, after which date it shall be disbanded.

snapshot.summary: Consult with multiple agencies and conduct outreach and education to food service establishments regarding the sidewalk and roadway cafe licensing process in the 6 most commonly spoken languages.
snapshot.quote: the department of transportation shall consult with agencies, commissions and offices including, but not limited to, the department of consumer and worker protection, the department of city planning, the department of environmental protection, the department of buildings, the department of design and construction, the department of health and mental hygiene, the department of parks and recreation, the department of sanitation, the fire department, the department of small business services, the landmarks preservation commission, the art commission, the office of emergency management, the mayor's office of media and entertainment, the mayor's office of people with disabilities, and the mayor's office of citywide event coordination and management, with respect to the adoption of such rules, as well as outreach and education targeted at food service establishments throughout the city in relation to the process for obtaining a license and revocable consent for sidewalk and roadway cafes, as well as relevant deadlines pertaining to application submissions and removal of any street furniture or materials in violation of rules promulgated pursuant to this local law. Such outreach and education shall be made available in the 6 most commonly spoken languages in the city pursuant to city planning.

snapshot.summary: Within 40 days of receiving a sidewalk cafe petition, either notify the public, hold a public hearing, and submit a written recommendation to the department, or waive the hearing and submit a recommendation.
snapshot.deadline_text: not later than 40 days after receipt of such petition
snapshot.quote: The community board shall, not later than 40 days after receipt of such petition

snapshot.summary: Order removal of furniture, equipment, structures or other obstructions used in unlicensed outdoor dining or in violation of design rules, providing opportunity to be heard.
snapshot.citation: Section 6 of the local law (NYC Admin. Code § 19-160.5(g))
snapshot.quote: The commissioner may order the removal of any furniture, equipment, structure or other obstruction used in connection with the operation of an outdoor dining area on the sidewalk or in the roadway by a person that is not licensed to operate a sidewalk cafe or roadway cafe pursuant to this subchapter and has no other lawful right to operate an outdoor dining area on such sidewalk or in such roadway or where any furniture, equipment, structure or other obstruction placed on the sidewalk or roadway by a licensee is inconsistent with criteria or design for such area as set forth in the rules of the department.
